question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{1}{16}x{y}^{3},\,0\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{X}(x).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/0a3aeba14383b64a0414f3163828d972102073dc972d64105e779b317b8574b0.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\frac{1}{16}x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{[\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{1}{64}{[x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{1}{64}[x\cdot (\sqrt{x})^{4}-x\cdot (\sqrt{0})^{4}] \\  & =\frac{1}{64}[x\cdot {x}^{2}-0] \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{3}}{64}, & 0\le x\le 4, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
